nodes.text: Build me a sparse traditional Korean hanok compound displayed on a large, perfectly flat square platform of pale gray checkerboard tiles, surrounded only by an open blue sky and distant featureless horizon. Place the architecture as a compact, orderly cluster near the platform’s center, leaving broad expanses of empty tiled ground around it. Form the main compound from roughly five connected or closely spaced single-story timber buildings arranged around small courtyards and narrow passages, with white plaster wall panels, warm brown exposed beams, low brick bases, wooden lattice windows and doors, and sweeping dark gray tiled roofs with raised eaves and decorative ridge ends. Include a prominent recessed entry passage containing a heavy double wooden gate studded with dark metal fittings and ring handles. Set two or three small detached pavilion-like outbuildings around the main cluster, including one isolated structure beside a long façade and another pair slightly farther away. Keep all structures low, rectilinear, and carefully aligned, but vary their roof orientations to create an interlocking silhouette. Use bright daylight, soft clouds, strong directional shadows, and no vegetation, furnishings, people, roads, fences, or surrounding landscape.
